legacy: A missing fillout may retain a token or throw by executor context.
projection: A missing reference is wrapped KALADA_REFERENCE_MISSING.
migration: Return Option.none explicitly when omission is intended.

legacy: Optional handling treats undefined as absent.
projection: undefined is not a Kalada value and is never omission.
migration: Normalize host input or return Option.none.

legacy: Exact substitution can return null.
projection: value emits null.
migration: Use a literal or JSON-valued expression.

legacy: Exact substitution can return false.
projection: value emits false.
migration: Do not wrap in Option.none.

legacy: Exact substitution can return 0.
projection: value emits 0.
migration: Do not use truthiness for omission.

legacy: Exact substitution can return an empty string.
projection: value emits the empty string.
migration: Strings are literal unless inside an explicit program AST.

legacy: Exact substitution can return an empty array.
projection: value emits a frozen empty array.
migration: Do not infer omission from length.

legacy: Exact substitution can return an empty object.
projection: value emits a frozen empty object.
migration: Do not infer omission from key count.

legacy: A whole-token fillout preserves the selected JSON value.
projection: value embeds a canonical program and preserves JSON type.
migration: Replace the token with a ref expression.

legacy: Tokens can be interpolated into surrounding text.
projection: All projection strings are literals; interpolation is invalid.
migration: Construct the final string in an approved core expression feature, if available.

legacy: A true condition selects its branch.
projection: The exact boolean true selects then.
migration: Embed a boolean-returning condition program.

legacy: A false condition advances to else.
projection: The exact boolean false selects else or omission.
migration: Use nested if nodes for chains.

legacy: Non-boolean truthy values select a branch.
projection: A non-boolean condition fails PROJECTION_CONDITION_TYPE.
migration: Produce an explicit boolean in core.

legacy: if/elseif/else selects the first truthy branch.
projection: Nested if nodes evaluate exact booleans in order and only select one branch.
migration: Lower each elseif to the else child of a nested if.

legacy: Optional keys omit false by truthiness.
projection: false is emitted; only Option.none omits.
migration: Return Option.none for the absent case.

legacy: Optional keys omit empty arrays and objects.
projection: Empty containers are emitted.
migration: Express optionality with Option.

legacy: No stable root omission envelope exists.
projection: Option.none returns the explicit omitted success variant.
migration: Handle omitted separately from a null output.

legacy: Array omission depends on executor behavior.
projection: Option.none contributes no slot and output stays dense.
migration: Use Option.none in the item node.

legacy: each/for traverses common arrays in enumeration order with an index-like binding.
projection: map traverses dense arrays left-to-right with a zero-based finite index.
migration: Use map with distinct item and index names.

legacy: Loop scope mutates objects/prototypes and can inherit memory.
projection: Nested lexical bindings shadow outer names before the host resolver.
migration: Name bindings explicitly; rely only on lexical scope.

legacy: for may enumerate object keys implicitly.
projection: map accepts only a dense JSON array.
migration: Provide an explicit ordered array.

legacy: merge combines object results.
projection: No node merges objects.
migration: Declare one ordered object with unique keys.

legacy: flatten/unwrap changes nested result shape.
projection: Arrays and maps never flatten implicitly.
migration: Construct the required shape explicitly.

legacy: include/template lookup injects registered templates.
projection: There is no include or external template lookup.
migration: Inline a canonical projection; modules remain deferred to #21.

legacy: let/lets stores mutable transform memory.
projection: Projection has no let node or mutable memory.
migration: Use core lexical expressions or explicit host references.

legacy: Template expressions can execute JavaScript-like source through Function.
projection: Only canonical data AST is evaluated; source is rejected.
migration: Translate approved logic to a canonical Kalada program.

legacy: Host functions can enter data/prototype paths.
projection: Callables cannot be resolved or emitted.
migration: Expose validated data only.

legacy: Property traversal can invoke getters and leak thrown errors.
projection: Accessors are rejected with a generic diagnostic and are never invoked.
migration: Supply own enumerable data properties.

legacy: Templates and runtime mutate or traverse prototypes.
projection: Unsafe keys are rejected and output objects have null prototypes.
migration: Rename unsafe keys before projection.

legacy: selecttransform-surikaterna is a CommonJS runtime package with runtime template machinery.
projection: The future optional @kalada/projection package has ESM/CJS exports, depends only on public core, and performs no prototype mutation.
migration: Adopt the future package explicitly; @kalada/core@0.4.0 remains unchanged.

legacy: Registered templates or host extensions can inject behavior.
projection: projection-v1 has no module, import, include, or hook contract.
migration: Track module/import design only in Kalada #21.
